final_candidates.decision_summary: Verified D at 473 (…L471-C472-D473-I-G-G…), the single conserved acidic residue of the OCT1 central cation-binding cavity (canonical Asp474) whose neutralization abolishes organic-cation binding and translocation. The small, chemically neutral Ala substitution minimally perturbs helix packing, so folding and membrane abundance are expected to be retained.

Verified W at 353 (…F347-I-L-M-Y-L-W353-F-T-D-S-V…), a pocket-lining tryptophan (canonical Trp354) providing cation-π/aromatic-box contacts for substrate recognition. Removing the indole should eliminate productive substrate binding while leaving the MFS bundle intact and well expressed.

Isosteric charge-neutralizing substitution at the same essential binding aspartate: side-chain volume and H-bonding capacity are conserved, maximizing the chance of normal folding/abundance, while the loss of negative charge removes the electrostatic driver of organic-cation binding. Kept over more speculative pocket mutants (E385A, Q446A, Y360A) because the mechanistic requirement for the D473 carboxylate is the strongest hypothesis in the pool.

stop_reason.detail: The candidate pool has converged and, without access to structural or functional evidence tools, additional self-review rounds are unlikely to alter the ranked Top-3.

history.rationale: Position 473 (D in TM11 'LCDIGG', equivalent to the canonical OCT1 Asp474) is the key acidic residue that coordinates the positive charge of organic cations; charge removal to Ala should abolish substrate translocation while an Asp->Ala change in a buried helix is generally well tolerated for folding/trafficking.

Verified D at 473 (LCD-IGG context); this is the conserved acidic residue of the central cation-binding cavity (canonical Asp474), whose neutralization abolishes organic cation binding while the small Ala substitution is unlikely to perturb the MFS fold.

Isosteric neutralization of the critical cation-coordinating Asp473 (canonical D474) removes the electrostatic anchor for substrates with minimal steric/packing perturbation, favoring retained membrane abundance.

Isosteric charge-neutralizing substitution at the same key binding aspartate; preserves side-chain volume/H-bonding so folding and abundance are very likely retained while the cation-attracting negative charge is removed.

Conservative charge-preserving change at the essential Asp473 that shifts carboxylate geometry by one methylene; reported to alter selectivity/strongly reduce turnover in OCT orthologs, but may retain partial transport.
Conservative Asp→Glu keeps the negative charge and typically only shifts substrate affinity rather than abolishing transport, which is orthogonal to the reward phenotype.

rejection.reason: Conservative Asp→Glu keeps the negative charge and typically only shifts substrate affinity rather than abolishing transport, which is orthogonal to the reward phenotype.

history.rationale: Trp353 (canonical W354) lies in the TM7 substrate-binding cleft and provides cation-pi/aromatic stacking for organic cations; Ala substitution should eliminate substrate recognition, though loss of a large buried aromatic carries some folding risk.

Verified W at 353 (…MYLW353FTDSV…), a pocket-lining tryptophan (canonical Trp354) repeatedly implicated in substrate recognition; promoted because loss of the aromatic cation-π contact should kill transport without global destabilization of the TM bundle.

Arg398 belongs to the conserved MFS 'A-motif' (D397-R398-V-G-R401) in the C-terminal half, whose salt-bridge network gates the rocker-switch conformational cycle; charge loss typically freezes transport while the protein still folds and reaches the membrane.

Verified R at 398 within the conserved cytoplasmic D397-R398-x-G-R motif that gates conformational cycling; demoted because motif-A/C-type charge-pair disruption frequently causes ER retention, conflicting with the abundance-preservation requirement.

Neutralizing the A-motif aspartate (D397 of DRxGR) breaks the inter-helical salt bridge required for alternating-access cycling; isosteric Asn minimizes destabilization so surface expression is likely preserved.

Redundant with R398A at the same intracellular DRxGR motif and, being only mildly perturbing, is more likely to give partial rather than null transport; dropped to make room for binding-site diversification.

rejection.reason: Redundant with R398A at the same intracellular DRxGR motif and, being only mildly perturbing, is more likely to give partial rather than null transport; dropped to make room for binding-site diversification.

history.rationale: Arg174 is the second arginine of the N-terminal A-motif (D170-R171-F-G-R174) that couples TM bundle movements; its removal should block the conformational cycle without grossly unfolding the transporter.
R174 lies in the MFS motif-A GRK element (G173-R174-K175) whose disruption predominantly destabilizes the fold and trafficking, violating the preserve-abundance constraint.

rejection.reason: R174 lies in the MFS motif-A GRK element (G173-R174-K175) whose disruption predominantly destabilizes the fold and trafficking, violating the preserve-abundance constraint.

history.rationale: Gln446 in TM10 faces the central cavity and is the human counterpart of the rat OCT1 affinity-determining Gln; truncation to Ala should remove a substrate hydrogen-bonding contact with modest structural cost.

Verified Q at 446 (…IAIQ446MICL…), corresponding to the rodent Oct1 pocket glutamine implicated in substrate selectivity; plausible affinity-abolishing but more likely to shift than eliminate transport.

Phe243 (canonical F244) contributes aromatic surface to the central binding pocket in OCT1 models; Ala substitution enlarges/deactivates the pocket and is a common way to kill binding while keeping the fold.
Verified F at 243 (…MAF243TVGLV…), a cavity-lining aromatic; Ala substitution may only enlarge the pocket rather than abolish translocation, so it stays mid-rank.

Trp216 (canonical W217) is a conserved cavity-lining aromatic implicated in cation binding in rat OCT1 mutagenesis; Ala removes the interaction but the large cavity created gives a moderate risk of reduced stability/abundance.

Verified W at 216 (…KGNW216MAGY…), the TM4 pocket tryptophan homologous to the rat Oct1 binding-site Trp; promoted from 0.38 because aromatic-box removal is a classic transport-null, expression-competent lesion.
